label: Each shared reader drops harness-injected text by construction: Pi never reads the custom_message entry type, Devin skips unflagged or system rows, DSH keeps only operator-source user messages, and OpenCode maps only text, reasoning and tool parts, so the brief cannot appear in records for any of them.

Pi stores the brief in a custom_message entry the reader discards, and briefDelivered reads only loaded.records, so the probe can never answer true for Pi; the committed unknown is a probe/log mismatch rather than a missing store.

OpenCode appends the brief in experimental.chat.system.transform, an in-memory transform that writes no session row, metric row or marker, so delivery on that runtime is not stored anywhere and a host upgrade could stop it silently.

One additive injected field on the load result, filled from entries each reader already parses then drops, makes Pi, Devin and DSH provable without changing the records contract every existing consumer reads.

OpenCode needs one written marker per delivered brief, reusing the advisor hook-diagnostic writer, because the transform is experimental and an OpenCode upgrade can remove it with no repository-side signal.

Codex is the one runtime whose honest delivery answer is false rather than unknown once the hook is registered and unapproved, and the rollout reader already keeps every payload role so the probe needs no new parsing.
